A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GraphRouter work. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original routing comparisons, experiments with newly introduced LLMs, and GNN sensitivity studies in Tables 4–5 and Figures 6–7.

after.justification: The original experiments are retained, and Appendix B adds results for an expanded benchmark and a restricted LLaMA-family model pool in Tables 22–23.

M1.justification: Section 2.3 and Algorithm 1 retain the same node initialization, heterogeneous aggregation, edge-label construction, training procedure, and inference rule. Appendix B evaluates the existing method without introducing a procedural adaptation.

E1.justification: Appendix B.1 extends the original Alpaca, GSM8K, SQuAD, and Multi-News coverage with HumanEval coding and HotpotQA multi-hop question answering. Tables 20 and 22 document their inclusion in the expanded evaluation, substantially broadening task coverage.

E2.justification: Tables 4–5 retain their comparator membership, and Table 22 reuses the original seven baselines. The new LLaMA-only experiment uses previously evaluated FrugalGPT and Oracle; it does not replace or remove comparators from an existing experiment.

E3.justification: The original protocols remain unchanged. Appendix B adds a 14-model evaluation pool, a separate six-LLaMA pool, and Pass@1 and EM metrics; the expanded benchmark retains the 70/10/20 query split. Its HumanEval sample count is unclear: B.1 describes 164 problems, while Table 20 reports 600 cases.

E4.justification: Appendix B.2 adds a focused test of whether GraphRouter distinguishes related LLaMA models, with comparisons against FrugalGPT and Oracle in Table 23. The original GNN dimension and depth sensitivity studies remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report averages over unspecified multiple evaluation rounds. The new tables follow this practice without adding run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Clarifying existing median markers in figure captions does not introduce a new estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Tables 22–23 add performance, cost, and reward results across three objectives for two additional settings; Tables 4–5 remain unchanged. For example, Performance First rewards are 0.393 versus Hybrid LLM's 0.350 in Table 22, and 0.422 versus FrugalGPT's 0.382 in Table 23. These are new-setting results. The latter implies about 10.5% improvement, rather than B.2's stated 10.8% minimum.

T1.justification: The aggregation equations, edge-prediction rule, and reward definition are unchanged. Neither version supplies formal theorems or proofs, and the later version adds none.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the claims of graph-based routing novelty, contextual modeling, multi-task applicability, and adaptation to new LLMs without retraining. The headline 12.3% and 9.5% improvement claims are unchanged; Appendix B supplies additional supporting experiments.

C2.justification: Section 6 newly identifies understanding numerical features such as token pricing and context length as an unresolved challenge for model representations. Appendix B.2 also interprets its results as evidence that interaction information distinguishes closely related LLMs. Existing limitations and mechanism explanations are retained.

D1.justification: The abstract changes code availability from a forthcoming release to a reported release at the same repository. Table 21 supplies sizes and token prices for four additional candidate LLMs. Existing training hyperparameters, software, hardware, and Appendix A descriptions are substantially unchanged.

R1.justification: The later version adds references on relational graph convolution, heterogeneous graph attention, numerical reasoning, and the two added datasets. These are focused additions; the comparison with prior routers and the central novelty positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Changes include small wording and cross-reference corrections, expanded figure explanations, a conference-publication header, and compact numbered presentation of the conclusion, limitations, and future work. Appendix B adds two subsections, while the existing narrative and section order remain largely intact.

P2.justification: The later version adds Tables 20–23, relocates Table 1, and redistributes Appendix A's description tables. Figures 2–4 receive clearer captions, and Figures 3–4 relabel their vertical axes from Effect to Performance. Existing diagrams, plotted findings, and principal table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: Appendix B provides useful broader task coverage and a focused test of discrimination among related models; clearer captions and the numerical-feature discussion also improve the paper. The gains are limited by reporting problems: HumanEval's 164-problem description is unreconciled with 600 reported cases, and Table 22's Oracle Balance reward is 0.171 although its displayed performance and cost imply 0.017 under the stated formula. These issues constrain confidence in the added evidence.
